This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA guidance and global model ensembles point to Manila highs of 34–36°C on May 24 amid easterly flow, scattered cloud cover, and a 10–20% chance of afternoon thunderstorms that can limit peak solar heating and introduce forecast spread. Typical May climatology shows daily maxima averaging near 34°C with high humidity, while urban heat-island effects in the metro area and exact timing of any convective cells differentiate outcomes between 35°C and 37°C. Trader consensus clusters on 36°C because short-range runs favor modest afternoon clearing before widespread rain develops. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model cycles will further refine these thresholds ahead of resolution.
